$schema_comment: BT-3261 shared conformance fixture. Every case here is consumed by BOTH crates/beamtalk-core/tests/section_divider_grammar_conformance.rs (calling parse_divider_name directly) and editors/vscode/src/__tests__/sectionDividerGrammar.test.ts (running the comment.line.double-slash.section-divider.beamtalk regex from editors/vscode/syntaxes/beamtalk.tmLanguage.json through the real Oniguruma engine). Add a case here — not to either test file individually — when either side's divider-recognition rule changes, so the two can never silently drift apart again. `content` is the already-`//`-stripped text parse_divider_name accepts (see its doc comment); the JS side reconstructs the raw source line as `// ` + content, the one canonical form both a hand-written divider and this fixture agree on.
